newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TAG Heuer 1996 sales rise 10.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: TAG Heuer 1996 sales rise 10.6 pct.

text.p: Swiss watchmaker TAG Heuer International SA said its sales in the year ended December 31, 1996, rose 10.6 percent to 419.7 million Swiss francs from 379.6 million in 1995.
In a statement, chief executive Christian Viros said that the company increased its average selling price per unit to 586 Swiss francs from 540 francs in the past year.
TAG Heuer also said it had signed an agreement to acquire its U.K. distributor Duval for an undisclosed amount.
"The acquisition will be financed from internal resources," it said.

The company, which floated its shares in September, said that it also expected a programme in which it will purchase its stock on the open market and award it to a group of about thirty managers to cost around four million Swiss francs.
The cost will be spread over a three year period.
